intro: You're looking for a small business bookkeeper near you because you'd rather spend your time running the business than chasing receipts and sorting out VAT. You want someone local who understands the pressures of an owner-managed firm and can take the paperwork off your hands. iComply introduces you to a suitable UK bookkeeper who quotes you directly, so you can compare and choose.
need_heading: What people searching for a small business bookkeeper near me usually need
need_lead: Most people who search for a small business bookkeeper near me are owner-managers who want reliable help with the day-to-day finances without taking on staff.
needs: You're spending evenings and weekends on invoices and receipts instead of growing the business.
You're not sure whether you're handling VAT correctly and want someone local to check and file for you.
You'd like a short monthly report that tells you how the business is doing without wading through spreadsheets.
You have unpaid invoices sitting on the system and want help chasing them politely and persistently.
You want to hand over the bookkeeping but keep your accountant for year-end accounts and tax advice.
context_heading: What to understand about bookkeeping for small businesses
context: Bookkeeping is not a regulated title in the UK, but anyone providing bookkeeping services for a fee must be supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes, either by HMRC or by a professional body. Membership of the Institute of Certified Bookkeepers (ICB) or the Association of Accounting Technicians (AAT) shows a bookkeeper has trained to a recognised standard and agreed to a code of conduct.

A good bookkeeper will be clear about where their work stops and your accountant's starts, particularly on year-end accounts and tax advice. Ask whether they hold professional indemnity insurance and which body supervises them, so you know you're dealing with someone accountable.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Describe your business and how many people work in it, so we can match you with a bookkeeper used to firms your size.
Say which bookkeeping tasks you want help with, such as sales invoices, purchase receipts, bank reconciliation or VAT returns.
Mention the accounting software you use, if any, so the bookkeeper can work with your existing records.
Explain how often you'd like reports or contact, for example a short monthly summary or a quarterly check-in.
Tell us whether you already have an accountant and where you see the bookkeeper's role ending.
Let us know your rough budget or what you're hoping to spend, so the bookkeeper can quote appropriately.
questions: Which professional body supervises you for anti-money-laundering purposes?
Do you hold professional indemnity insurance?
How will you keep me informed about my finances each month?
Will you chase unpaid invoices on my behalf, and how do you approach that?
Where does your work stop and my accountant's begin on year-end accounts and tax?
Can you work with the accounting software I already use?

faqs.q: Do I need a bookkeeper if I already have an accountant?
faqs.a: Many small businesses use a bookkeeper for the day-to-day records and an accountant for year-end accounts and tax advice. A bookkeeper can keep things tidy so your accountant's time is spent on the higher-level work. It's worth asking each to be clear about where their work stops and the other's starts.

faqs.q: What does a small business bookkeeper near me actually do?
faqs.a: Typically they record sales and purchase invoices, reconcile bank statements, keep receipts in order and may prepare VAT returns. They can also chase unpaid invoices and give you a short monthly report. The exact scope depends on what you agree with them.

faqs.q: How do I judge if a bookkeeper is right for my small business?
faqs.a: Ask about their training and which body supervises them, such as the Institute of Certified Bookkeepers (ICB) or the Association of Accounting Technicians (AAT). Check they hold professional indemnity insurance and are clear about where their work stops and an accountant's begins. A good bookkeeper will also explain things in plain language and answer your questions openly.

faqs.q: Can a bookkeeper help me get on top of VAT?
faqs.a: Yes, many small business bookkeepers handle VAT records and prepare VAT returns as part of their service. They should be supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes and will work within the scope you agree. If you're unsure about VAT rules, ask them to explain what they can and can't do.
